caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1144 of 1998
lawyer:
AKM Zahirul Haque, Advocate with the leave of the Court, instructed by Sharifuddin Chaklader, Advocate-on-Record — For the Petitioners. 
Not Represented — Respondents.
parties:
Abdul Barek and another ------- Petitioner
Vs.
Radha Madhab Mridha and ors ------- Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Abdur Rouf J: The decree-holder-respondents got a contested decree on 16-2-71 for reconveyance of the suit land in Title Suit No. 11 of 1970 from the Second Court of Munsif. Narayanganj against the defendants named therein and in pursuance thereof got the required deed of reconveyance on 22-3-75 in Title Execution Case No. 10 of 1972 through Court. Subsequently the decree-holders prayed to the executing court for possession in the suit land with the help of police force. In the meantime the present petitioners and respondent No. 8-10, as third parties, instituted Title Suit No. 242 of 1978 in the second Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for cancellation of the aforesaid decree which was renumbered as Title Suit No. 258 of 1981 on being transferred to the Court of Subordinate Judge, Narayanganj. The third parties on 23-1-79 also filed an application under section 47 CPC in the said execution case for its rejection. By an order dated 12-5-81 the executing court allowed the said application under section 47 CPC ex parte although the Court had earlier fixed 17-6-81 for hearing the said application. The decree-holders on 25-4-87 filed an application under section 151 CPC in the said executing court for recalling the ex parte order dated 12-5-81 and re-hearing the matter assigning reasons that they had no knowledge of the date of hearing of the said application filed under section 47 CPC. The executing Court by its order dated 23-9-87 rejected the application holding, inter alia, that although the order had been passed earlier for hearing of decree-holders'' application on 17-6-81 and the same was not communicated to them but it is unbelievable that during the long period of more than 5 years they had no knowledge of the said order dated 12-5-81. 

 2. The aggrieved decree-holders then moved the High Court Division under section 115 CPC against the said order of the executing Court and obtained a Rule, Civil Revision No. 4042 of 1997. A learned Single Judge of the High Court Division by the impugned judgment and order dated 25-8-98 upon making the Rule absolute set aside the aforesaid order of the executing court and therefore the execution case shall now proceed in accordance with law. 

 5. It is true that determination of any question within section 47 CPC shall be deemed to be a ''decree'' as is defined in section 2(2) CPC and therefore against the order dated 12-5-81 an appeal would lie in the Court of District Judge. 

 7. So far as the instant case is concerned the executing court had earlier passed an order fixing 17-6-81 as the date for hearing the objection raised by the present petitioners and respondent Nos. 8-10 under section 47 CPPC. But later on without recalling such order or even without assigning any reason and under misapprehension of facts and also on being mislead by the objectors wrongly heard and allowed the said objection in the absence of the decree-holders and behind their back, who had acquired a vested right to get the decree in question executed against the judgment-debtors.
